body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Thursday, November 5, and the big local story is the city council's unanimous approval of the Riverview Marketplace zoning change, clearing the way for the Whole Foods-anchored center at Coffee Road and Rosedale Highway. Outside, expect a high near 69 under clear skies, with air quality sitting at a moderate 82 and no weather alerts anywhere in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

The small hours opened with an armed robbery on Highway 46, where deputies were sent at 12:11 a.m. to a gas station on the 21,900 block after two masked juveniles, at least one of them armed, took cash from the register and from a customer before running east on foot toward a nearby restaurant.

Weapons calls carried much of the night. A driver reported a man who brandished a firearm from a white Honda at 1:55 a.m., and an officer was searching a call for suspected drugs and weapons at 9:51 p.m.

Violence kept officers moving. They were sent to the 8300 block of California Avenue at 10:10 p.m., where a man was reported to have hit his head on a wall during an argument with his father and was not moving; to Gilmore Avenue and Buck Owens Boulevard in north Bakersfield at 3:47 a.m., where a man was reported to have pepper-sprayed the caller over a payment dispute; and to an assault at an Elmwood Avenue home in east Bakersfield at 6:50 a.m.

Three pursuits crossed the night — a car that fled an officer east on Pioneer Drive in east Bakersfield at 9:44 p.m. and was lost, a traffic stop on Castro Lane that became a chase onto Highway 99 at 12:25 a.m., and a wrong-way driver on Highway 99 who was spun with a PIT maneuver at 2:06 a.m. but kept creeping along. The worst crash came in the dark, a single vehicle that rolled onto its roof on the 8,100 block of Old River Road in southwest Bakersfield at 4:52 a.m., with the driver out of the car and the patients refusing a hospital.

Fire crews had two calls of their own: a fire of unknown origin in a mechanic's yard on South Union Avenue between White Lane and Pacheco Road at 9:55 p.m., and an outside fire in the alley behind Tulare Street in east Bakersfield at 3:08 a.m. Earlier in the evening, crews were sent to a person who fell and was unconscious near Au Chocolat Drive at 7:15 p.m., and the CHP was told about a pedestrian in the northbound lanes of Highway 99 just north of the airport at 7:56 p.m.

## Today's weather

It's currently 50 degrees at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 69 this afternoon and a low around 51 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are burning. Air quality is 82, which lands in the moderate range — fine for most of us, though if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, it's a reasonable day to keep an eye on how you feel during longer stretches outside. Otherwise, it's a quiet, seasonable valley Thursday.

## Top stories

**The Bakersfield City Council voted unanimously Wednesday night to approve a zoning change for the Riverview Marketplace shopping center, 23ABC reports.** The proposed center sits on the southwest corner of Coffee Road and Rosedale Highway, on the site of a former PG&E power station, and the land needed its designation changed on paper before the project could keep moving. Whole Foods was announced as the main anchor back in January 2024. City Manager Christian Clegg called it a notable redevelopment with real positive impacts for the surrounding community, adding that important mitigations have been planned for. Most public comment Wednesday supported approval, though Aidan Marshall of Californians Allied for a Responsible Economy asked the council to hold off, pointing to Valley Fever concerns from disturbing 46 acres of soil next to a senior community. Supporters say those concerns have been addressed.

**Sixteen people at Wasco State Prison walked out of a classroom Wednesday with job certifications and a plan for life after release, according to 23ABC.** The graduates completed a vocational program run through CalCTRA, which trains incarcerated people in trades including facilities maintenance, data entry, and industrial skills. Graduate Rafiki Bogar said the program instills confidence and gives people the mentality to go get a job — and keep it. Formerly incarcerated CalCTRA alum Justin Ennis spoke at the ceremony about using his training to start his own business, and director Suzie Changus said much of the value is soft-skill work: showing up, acting professionally, taking direction, and learning how to interview. CalCTRA says 85% of its graduates do not return to prison.

**Randy Villegas is projected to win California's 22nd Congressional District, unofficially unseating incumbent David Valadao, 23ABC reports.** Villegas told the station his support came from Republicans, Democrats, and independents alike, and that his top priorities in Washington are expanding access to healthcare and lowering the cost of living — including restoring Medicaid funding and co-sponsoring Medicare for all on day one. One Kern County resident told 23ABC that party mattered less to him than electing leaders who will stand up for human rights. The station reached out to Valadao's office and did not receive a response.

**KGET 17 reports that Bakersfield police are searching for a man who threatened a GET bus passenger with a machete.** No further details were available in the headline alone.

**According to KGET 17, a five-day campaign pushed Paula Dahl to an early lead in the Kern Community College District board race.** The race remains early, and no further details were available beyond the headline.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Xavier Becerra is projected to succeed Gavin Newsom as California governor, and that he has vowed to fight Trump.** No further details were available beyond the headline.

## Something good

Sixteen men at Wasco State Prison spent months earning job certifications through CalCTRA, and Wednesday they graduated with trades in hand — facilities maintenance, data entry, industrial skills — and something harder to certify: the confidence to walk into an interview and ask for the job. One graduate, Rafiki Bogar, put it simply, saying the program helps people build belief in themselves. A former graduate who now runs his own business came back to tell them it can be done. That's a good morning's work, and a good reason to smile.

## Coming up this week

The Bakersfield Planning Commission meets tonight, Thursday, November 5, at 5:30 p.m. — the week's one scheduled public meeting, and worth a look if you follow land use around town.

The Fox Theater has a busy stretch ahead. Journey USA takes the stage Saturday, November 7, sharing the date with TEXAS TORNADO TRADITION. Sunday, November 8, brings the 2026 Golden Empire Youth Cheer EXPO, and Monday, November 9, the Cults & Classics series screens "Play Misty for Me." Looking a little further out, NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives November 13, and the Cults & Classics Season Pass for 2026–2027 is already on sale for next year's slate.

If you're planning around the weather, today's the easy one — mild, calm, and clear. Get out and enjoy it while it lasts.

top.title: Bakersfield City Council unanimously approves zoning change for Riverview Marketplace shopping center
